source.title: The Shaped Transformer: Attention Models in the Infinite Depth-and-Width Limit
source.authors: Lorenzo Noci; Chuning Li; Mufan Bill Li; B. He; T. Hofmann; Chris J. Maddison; Daniel M. Roy

record.file_problem: Full paper text provided, including appendices; no apparent truncation or garbling that prevents reading.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports preliminary Transformer training experiments and training loss outcomes, which bear on whether its proposed shaped architecture is trainable. It does not test the listed claim versions about classification error on CIFAR, local minima, initialization effects on plain networks, learning-rate stability thresholds, or batch-normalization speed.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the paper's own masked-language-model pretraining loss results and GLUE fine-tuning evaluation. Covariance and gradient stability results concern initialization and are outside the listed claim versions. Cited findings from prior work are not extracted as rows.
record.test_reason: The study uses signal-propagation principles to design shaped attention and reports its own architecture's performance. Its covariance and gradient measurements at initialization are proxies for trainability; its training experiments compare residual Transformers with different attention mechanisms. Neither tests initialization-dependent learning in plain networks, batch normalization, or the other specified versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors present initialization theory and simulations, and preliminary training results showing comparable masked-language-model losses to a Pre-LN baseline. They also describe approximately comparable training speed without LayerNorm, while explicitly reserving practical feasibility for broader evaluation.
record.recipe_differences: The study modifies Softmax attention and uses masked-language-model pretraining; its preliminary experiments do not apply the claim's CIFAR classification-error recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports training loss separately by depth (d = 18 or 24), shaped-attention variant (Learn or Recover), and γ; it also states larger γ values produced loss divergence. The appendix reports a learning-rate grid and best-run losses.

fits_no_version.finding: At 100K steps, shaped Transformer variants have masked-language-model training losses comparable to the Pre-LN baseline across the reported depths and residual strengths.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Learn and Recover shaped attention variants can attain masked-language-model losses comparable to a Pre-LN Transformer under the tested training recipe.

fits_no_version.finding: Figures 1–4 show that attention shaping prevents token alignment and stabilizes initialization gradients under the tested settings; these are initialization measurements rather than learning-speed or trainable-depth outcomes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Shaping attention can preserve token covariance and gradient propagation at initialization in deep residual attention networks.

fits_no_version.finding: Appendix D and Figure 6 report baseline Softmax entropy collapse at learning rate 0.001, while the Recover variant avoids it; larger initial residual strengths also cause loss divergence.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Attention shaping and residual-strength choices affect Transformer entropy stability and training divergence in the reported recipe.

record.problems: The authors call the training experiments preliminary and state that limited computing resources constrained the experiments. Reported results use one language-modeling dataset subset and two depths; losses are averaged over four random seeds and the best run over a learning-rate grid. They do not report classification error.
record.rows_left_out: No rows left out. Table 2 reports downstream GLUE evaluation metrics after fine-tuning, but those are not training classification errors for the claim and are not extracted as claim-bearing results.

untested.parts: Training classification error in convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/100, including random or corrupted labels and effects of size, stopping and regularization.
Spurious local minima in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems and their reduction by extra student neurons.
Depth-dependent training-error degradation in plain convolutional networks, its prevention by identity shortcuts, and the specified tanh and Fixup exceptions.

Initialization-dependent training speed and trainable depth in plain networks, including orthogonal versus Gaussian weights and very deep convolutional networks. Initialization covariance and gradient stability in modified residual Transformers do not measure these outcomes.

Loss recovery, curvature evolution and divergence relative to a measured learning-rate stability threshold. Softmax entropy collapse and divergence at larger residual strength do not establish these effects.

Batch-normalization effects on accuracy gain and learning-rate tolerance, and comparable training without normalization using Fixup. The study compares shaped Transformers against a layer-normalized baseline.

record.verdict_notes: The record's tests/T2 classification conflicts with its correct assessment that no listed version is tested. All 14 training-loss values match Table 1. They can remain as contextual method-performance results, but cannot support verdicts on V1–V6. No omitted claim-bearing result was identified.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 classification error, random or corrupted labels, model size, early stopping and regularization recipes.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student optimization and student width relative to teacher width.
Plain versus residual convolutional network training error as depth increases; shortcuts and normalization comparisons for classification.
Initialization-dependent training speed or trainable depth for plain networks, including tanh and very deep convolutional networks.
Training trajectories and divergence behavior as learning rate crosses a stability threshold in squared-loss or full-batch settings.
Batch-normalization effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and direct Fixup comparison.
